ref.substituent_description: A benzene ring has EtOOC at one carbon and, para to it, a CH=C(CH3) alkene; the alkene carbon bearing a methyl is bonded to the aromatic ring of a tetrahydronaphthalene. That aromatic carbon is separated by one CH from the ring-fusion carbon attached to the top C(CH3)2; the saturated ring has two methyl stubs on each of the two carbons next to the aromatic ring (four methyls in total) and two CH2 between them.
ref.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: alkene (1), benzene (3), tetralin aromatic ring (3). Methyls are drawn only as bond stubs: one on the alkene carbon and four on the tetralin ring. No E/Z label written.

wrong.substituent_description: A circle-depicted benzene ring has, at one position, a carbonyl carbon (drawn as =O above and OEt below) and, para (position 4) to it, a vinyl linkage CH=C(line methyl)-; the alkene carbon bearing a short methyl line is bonded to a second circle-depicted benzene ring at the ring carbon directly adjacent to a ring-fusion carbon. That benzene ring is fused to a saturated six-membered ring whose two carbons next to the fusion each carry two short unlabelled lines (four methyl lines in total: two on the carbon at the top, two on the carbon at the bottom right).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The carbonyl carbon is drawn as a curled C-like stroke, probably a written C label
The t of OEt is written like a plus sign
The aromatic circles are irregular teardrop or D shapes
Methyl lines have small hooked tips and carry no label
The vinyl-bearing carbon of the second ring is attached adjacent to a ring-fusion carbon (exact position on that ring is slightly hard to judge from hand-drawn hexagon)
wrong.notes: Handwritten black ink on white. Double bonds: one C=O (two vertical strokes) and one alkene C=C (inner short line). The tetralin-like ring system has two aromatic-style circles plus a saturated ring with four plain line substituents.

correct.substituent_description: A circled benzene ring carries EtOOC at one carbon and, para (1,4) to it, a CH=C(stub) alkene whose far carbon carries one unlabelled line stub (methyl) and is bonded to a second circled benzene ring. That second benzene ring is fused to a saturated six-membered ring; the ring attachment to the alkene is on the carbon two bonds from a fusion carbon, and the two saturated carbons next to the fusion carbons each carry two unlabelled line stubs (four methyl-type stubs in total).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Unlabelled short line stubs (one on the alkene carbon and four on the saturated ring carbons) are drawn as plain lines with no Me label.
The first O of EtOOC is a tall oval, written like a D/O.
correct.notes: Handwritten. Alkene C=C drawn with one inner double-bond line; no E/Z label. Two aromatic circles.

ref.substituent_description: A benzene ring bears EtOOC on one vertex and, at the para vertex, a CH=C(CH3)- unit (the C=C double bond is drawn, with a plain methyl line on the carbon attached to the second aryl). That second aryl is the aromatic ring of a tetrahydronaphthalene fused to a saturated 6-membered ring that has two quaternary carbons, each bearing two methyl lines (four methyls in total); the vinyl carbon is attached to the aromatic carbon adjacent to the CH that sits next to a ring-fusion carbon (position 2 of the 5,5,8,8-tetramethyl-5,6,7,8-tetrahydronaphthalene).
ref.notes: Typeset structure. Double bonds: 3 in the phenyl, 3 in the tetralin aromatic ring, 1 C=C. All methyls are unlabeled plain lines. No stereo descriptors written.

wrong.substituent_description: A peptide-like chain: H2N-C(=O)-NH-CH2CH2-CH(bold wedge to NH)-... and an iPr (bold wedge) / NHBoc substituted alpha carbon with a C(=O) bonded to that NH; the NH is then bonded to CH2-C(=O)-HN attached to a benzene ring (aromatic circle). On that ring the HN is on one carbon, a CH2OH on the carbon para to it, and a CH2-N(Me)-C(=O)-O-CH2 on the carbon adjacent to the CH2OH carbon (meta to the HN); the CH2 ends at a fluorene (9-fluorenyl) group with two aromatic-circle benzene rings and a five-membered ring.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Exact ring positions of CH2OH and CH2N(Me) relative to the HN on the middle benzene ring are hard to be certain of
The upper bold wedge sits between the chain carbon and the NH nitrogen; its narrow end and the stereocentre it belongs to are unclear
H of the NH is written below N; NHBoc written as one label
wrong.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white. Double bonds: 4 C=O (urea, two amides, carbamate).

correct.substituent_description: A para-disubstituted benzene ring (circle) has EtOOC at one position and, para to it, a CH=C(CH3) vinyl group (one C=C, methyl drawn as an unlabelled line on the second alkene carbon). The alkene carbon bearing the methyl is attached to an aromatic ring (circle) that is fused to a saturated six-membered ring carrying two gem-dimethyl carbons (four unlabelled methyl lines, one pair on each carbon adjacent to the ring fusion on opposite sides), i.e. a tetramethyl-tetrahydronaphthalene attached at a beta position (meta to one fusion carbon, para to the other).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: first O of EtOOC looks like a D
ring bonds are irregular so ring junction details are hard to confirm
correct.notes: Handwritten. Only one double bond (the alkene); the benzene rings are drawn with circles. Methyl groups are unlabelled line ends.
